question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the staff-to-child ratio for infants aged 6 weeks to 18 months? Give the number of infants per staff member.
quote: 6 weeks to 18 months (infants) ... 1 staff member to 5 infants
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Maximum group size for infants is 10 (2.217(A)(15)). Toddlers 12-36 months are also 1:5 (group 10); groups of 24-36 months are 1:7 (group 14).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the staff-to-child ratio for a group of children aged 3 years to 4 years? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: 3 years to 4 years ... 1 staff member to 10 children
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). The chart's adjoining band '2-1/2 years to 3 years' is 1:8, so a child just turning 3 sits at the boundary. Max group size for 3-4 years is 20. A mixed group of 2 1/2 to 6 years is 1:10; at nap time the ratio may be doubled for children 2 1/2 and older if conditions in 2.217(A)(10) are met.

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the staff-to-child ratio for a group of children aged 4 years to 5 years? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: 4 years to 5 years ... 1 staff member to 12 children
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Max group size 24. In other preschool age mixes, the youngest child's ratio applies if more than 20% of the group is younger (2.217(A)(14)(a)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the staff-to-child ratio for children 5 years and older (outside formal kindergarten class sessions)? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: 5 years and older ... 1 staff member to 15 children
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). '5 years and older' is the oldest band in the center chart (max group 30). Formal kindergarten class sessions may run 1:25 (2.217(A)(11)). Separately licensed school-age child care centers (section 2.500) also use one staff member per 15 children, max group 30 (2.510(D)-(E)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the maximum group size for children aged 4 years to 5 years?
quote: Maximum Group Size for Children ... 4 years to 5 years ... 24 children
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Group size in preschool and school-age classrooms may be exceeded for circle time, meal and snack time, special occasions and activities, but licensed room capacity may never be exceeded (2.217(A)(15)(c)-(d)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the minimum age for an early childhood teacher assigned responsibility for a group of children?
quote: An early childhood teacher, assigned responsibility for a single group of children and working under the supervision of a director, must be at least eighteen (18) years of age
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Staff aides may be 16 (infant staff aides 18) but must work under the supervision of the director or an early childhood teacher (2.216(G)). 2.217(A)(1) says only staff/volunteers qualified under 2.216(A) who work directly with children are counted in ratios.

question: For the director of a large licensed child care center in Colorado (16 or more children, 8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200), how many months of verified experience caring for children are required if the person has no degree but has completed the 30 semester credit hours of required early childhood coursework?
quote: Persons who have no degree but have completed the thirty (30) semester credit hours specified in rule section 2.214(B)(2), must have six (6) months (910 hours) of verified experience
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Experience is caring for 4 or more unrelated children under 8 (910 hours). Directors with a bachelor's or higher in a listed field, or an ECE professional credential level III, need no extra experience; associate's degree in ECE/child development needs 3 months. All large center directors need a Department director qualifications letter or a level III+ credential before working (2.214(A)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), how many clock hours of ongoing professional development must each staff member who works with children complete each year?
quote: All staff who work with children must complete a minimum of fifteen (15) clock hours of ongoing professional development each year
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). At least 3 of the 15 hours per year must focus on social-emotional development. The year runs from the employee's start date; hours cannot be carried over.

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the minimum open indoor play space required per child (for preschool-age and older children)?
quote: There must be open, indoor play space of at least thirty (30) square feet of floor space per child
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Infant and toddler rooms differ by use: infants 35 sq ft in a separate play area or 50 sq ft for combined sleep/play; toddlers 30 sq ft separate play or 45 sq ft combined (2.231(A) table).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the minimum outdoor play space per child for preschool-age and older children using the play area at one time?
quote: The outdoor learning environment for preschool age and older must provide a minimum of seventy-five (75) square feet of space per child for a group of children using the total play area at any one time
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Per child using the area at one time. The total play area must also hold at least 33% of licensed capacity for preschool age and older, or 1,500 sq ft, whichever is greater. Infant play areas must be at least 400 sq ft; toddler areas 750 sq ft (10 toddlers) or 1,050 sq ft (14+).

question: In a licensed family child care home in Colorado (8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.300), what is the maximum temperature of a child's bath water?
quote: When a child is bathing, the bath water must be between ninety (90) and one hundred and twenty (120) degrees
notes: Facility type: family child care home (section 2.300), not child care centers. This is bath water (range 90-120 degrees; the rule text says only 'degrees', without a scale). The child care center rules (2.200) set no hot water temperature limit for sinks/taps; they only require hot water pipes to be insulated or out of children's reach (2.237(F)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is required before staff give a child any routine prescription or over-the-counter medication?
answer: A current written order from a health care provider with prescriptive authority and written parental consent
quote: Any unexpired routine medication, prescription or non-prescription (over the counter), must be administered only with a current written order of a health care provider with prescriptive authority and with written parental consent
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Applies to over-the-counter medication too. Home remedies, homeopathic medication, vitamins and supplements must not be given. Long-term authorizations must be renewed at least annually (2.220(E)); staff giving medication need Department-approved medication administration training and delegation.

question: How often must fire drills be held at a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200)?
quote: Fire drills must be held monthly and be consistent with local fire department procedures
notes: Rule is in the General Rules for Child Care Facilities (2.100), which apply to child care centers (2.202). Emergency, lockdown and active shooter drills are at least quarterly; tornado drills monthly from March to October.

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), for at least how long must a child's records be kept after the child's last date of attendance?
quote: The records of children and staff must be maintained by the center for at least three (3) years after the last date of attendance or employment with the program
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Staff records likewise 3 years after the last date of employment. Enrollment and daily attendance/arrival-departure records: the past 12 months on file at the center and the previous 2 years at the center or a central location (2.211(F)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), in what position must an infant be placed for sleep?
quote: An infant must be placed on their back for sleeping
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Alternative sleep positions only with a health care plan completed and signed by the child's physician (2.223(C)(10)).

question: Within how many hours must a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200) report to the Colorado Department of Early Childhood a child's injury that requires medical attention by a health care professional?
quote: An injury to a child that requires medical attention by a health care professional or admission to a hospital, whether or not treatment was given. This report must be completed in the online injury system within 24 hours of an incident
notes: General Rules (2.100), applying to centers and other facility types. Report goes to the licensing agency (Department). 2.124(A)(1) says the 24 hours exclude weekends and holidays, or run from the child's return to the facility. Paper form if the online system is unavailable.

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), when must the parent provide proof of the child's immunization status or an exemption?
answer: Prior to or on the first day of admission
quote: Colorado law requires proof of immunization status or exemption be provided prior to or on the first day of admission
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). The center may refuse to admit a child without documentation of immunization status or exemption (2.219(A)). Nonmedical exemptions need a signed certificate from a Colorado immunizing provider or the CDPHE online education module certificate.

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), at least one staff member with current First Aid and CPR certification must be on duty for every how many children in attendance?
quote: For every thirty (30) or fewer children in attendance, there must be at least one (1) staff member on duty who holds a current Department-approved First Aid and Safety certificate, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for all ages of children
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Certified staff must be with the children at all times, and at each location if children are split up. Toddler programs need one certified staff member per 15 or fewer toddlers (2.216(C)(3)). Other caregivers must complete the Introduction to First Aid and CPR module within 30 days (2.213(F)).

question: In the toddler room of a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the minimum distance required between cribs or cots?
quote: In the toddler room, a crib, sleeping cot, or two (2) inch mat must be provided for each child, and there must be a minimum of two (2) feet between each crib or cot
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Preschool cots or pads must also be spaced at least 2 feet apart on all sides during rest time (2.223(D)). For infant rooms the rule only requires cribs to be arranged so all infants are easily accessible to staff (2.231).

question: Under Colorado's general rules for child care facilities (8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.100), which apply to licensed child care centers, how long does a permanent license remain in effect?
answer: Until it is surrendered or revoked (no fixed expiration)
quote: The permanent license remains in effect until surrendered or revoked
notes: Applies to all facility types under 8 CCR 1402-1, including child care centers. The licensee must submit an annual declaration of compliance/continuation notice and annual fee (2.107(B)). A provisional license may be issued only for the initial six-month licensing period (2.108(A)).

question: In a preschool classroom of children aged 3 years to 4 years at a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), if all conditions for nap time are met (at least half asleep, another staff member onsite, group size and room capacity not exceeded, qualified staff supervising), how many children may one staff member supervise at nap time?
quote: At nap time, the child to staff ratio may be doubled for children two and one half (2 ½) years of age and older in preschool classrooms ... 3 years to 4 years ... 1 staff member to 10 children
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Doubling applies only to children 2 1/2 and older in preschool classrooms, when at least half the children are sleeping, another staff member is onsite and immediately available, group size and room capacity are not exceeded, and the supervising staff member is an early childhood teacher or assistant early childhood teacher.

question: During formal kindergarten class sessions at a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the staff-to-child ratio? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: Formal kindergarten class sessions must have one (1) staff member for each twenty-five (25) or fewer children in attendance
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). At other times of the day the ratio for these children is 1:15.

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), in a mixed preschool-age group other than the 2 1/2-to-6-year mixed group, above what percentage of younger children in the group must the ratio for the youngest child be used?
quote: In other preschool age combinations, the staff ratio for the youngest child must be utilized if more than twenty percent (20%) of the group is composed of younger children
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Applies when more than 20% are younger. Does not apply to infants and toddlers; toddler groups always use the youngest child's ratio. A mixed group of 2 1/2 to 6 years has its own ratio of 1:10 (max group 20). The same 20% rule applies to group size (2.217(A)(15)(a)).

question: In a licensed school-age child care center in Colorado (8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.500) that has been cited for lack of supervision, operating out of ratio, or operating without sufficient qualified staff, what staff-to-child ratio must it keep whenever 4-year-olds are present? Give the number of children per staff member.
quote: the school-age child care center must maintain a 1:12 staff to child ratio with a max group size of twenty-four (24) children any time four (4) year olds are present
notes: Facility type: school-age child care center (section 2.500). Normal ratio is 1:15 with max group 30 (2.510(D)-(E)). The center may return to normal ratios after one year with no further such violations (2.510(F)(1)).

question: In a licensed child care center in Colorado (a center providing less than 24-hour care under 8 CCR 1402-1, section 2.200), what is the minimum age for a staff aide working in the infant program?
quote: Infant staff aides must be at least eighteen (18) years of age
notes: Facility type: child care center (8 CCR 1402-1 section 2.200). Other staff aides may be 16 (2.216(G)(1)). Infant program staff aides must also complete 8 hours of orientation and work under direct supervision (2.216(B)).
